dailyInsight.headline: Audit pre-trust startup paths for workspace-owned helpers
dailyInsight.insight: Codex's public main-branch change treats automatic startup and diagnostics as work that must stay safe before a repository is trusted. Source-build and fork operators can test that boundary without touching a production workspace: put harmless marker helpers early in a disposable workspace PATH, then exercise startup, `codex doctor --json`, and any automatic curated-plugin sync. The marker should never run; an unavailable trusted helper should produce the conservative fallback rather than a workspace-selected executable.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The change resolves helpers used before trust from trusted system installation directories, stops `doctor` from running PATH-selected programs merely to inspect them, and gives curated-plugin Git subprocesses a sanitized environment. Its black-box test creates workspace `node_modules/.bin` marker helpers for commands including git, curl, rg, tmux, and npm, then checks startup, doctor, feedback-log collection, and plugin sync without allowing a marker to execute.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A workspace is not meaningfully untrusted if a convenience check can execute a program that the workspace selected first. This is a practical audit of a boundary that can otherwise hide in startup and support tooling rather than in an obvious tool call.

actions.audience: Codex source-build or fork operators, and builders of comparable workspace-aware coding agents
actions.label: Run a disposable pre-trust helper audit
actions.instruction: Create a disposable untrusted repository with harmless marker helpers early in its workspace-controlled PATH. Exercise startup, `codex doctor --json`, and any automatic curated-plugin synchronization. Confirm the markers do not run and a missing trusted helper takes a conservative fallback. Do not use production credentials, a real plugin checkout, or a live workspace.

receipts.title: Avoid executing PATH helpers before workspace trust (#42324)
receipts.supports: The public change states that automatic startup and `codex doctor` can run before trust, moves helper resolution to trusted system locations, sanitizes plugin-sync Git, and adds hostile-PATH coverage.

receipts.title: Hostile-PATH startup and doctor safety test
receipts.supports: The test plants marker helpers in a repository-controlled PATH and verifies that startup and doctor do not execute them while still reporting inspected locations.

receipts.title: Trusted system executable resolver
receipts.supports: The resolver limits pre-trust executable selection to platform system installation directories rather than ambient workspace PATH entries.

confidence.basis: A fresh public commit, explicit resolver implementation, sanitized startup path, and black-box hostile-PATH tests agree on one small reversible audit.

dailyInsight.limitation: These receipts establish intended main-branch source behavior and tests. They do not prove that a tagged or deployed release contains the change, that every downstream wrapper or helper is protected, or that a particular workspace had an exploitable helper.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise or withdraw this call if public source or a regression shows a workspace-PATH helper executes before trust, or that automatic curated-plugin Git inherits such a helper path.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for a tagged release carrying the change and for cross-platform regression coverage that demonstrates the trusted resolver and conservative fallbacks on the packaged distributions operators actually run.
